name: In-Page Navigation
summary: In-page navigation is a list of links to sections of the page you are already on. Use it when a long document needs a way in other than scrolling. Following a link moves the keyboard only if the target can take focus, so one attribute on the heading decides whether the jump landed.
demoNote: Everything under Common mistakes is live. Press a link in example 2 and the readout prints what the browser actually gave focus to; every number on this page is measured rather than claimed.

contract.useWhen: In-page links to sections, where focus has to actually land on the target.
keyboard: native: after the jump the next stop is inside the target — if it took focus
native: follows the focused link, which is the jump
failureModes: no tabindex=-1 on the target, so the page scrolls and the next Tab starts from the top
tabindex=0 on the target, which buys a Tab stop on every heading in the document
scroll-margin-top of 0, which parks the heading under the sticky header (SC 2.4.11)
two nav landmarks with no aria-label, indistinguishable in a landmark menu
the active section written to a live region per scroll event — throttle it
api: AC.createJumpNav(root, options) -> { links, targets, current, destroy }
